eligibility_rationale: Floral methoxypyrazines are assayed for florivore response, but no direct pollinator response or common plant reproductive outcome is measured.
Nectar robbing is the experimental context and alters staminode screening mechanics; antagonists are not measured as responding to an independently declared floral coordinate A.
Stamen modules support pollinating versus pollen-feeding functions by the same bees, but no common plant reproductive outcome links the two routes.
Soil/pathogen legacy alters floral phenotype and bee visitation; the pathogen is an antecedent context rather than a receiver of the same floral coordinate.
Herbivory changes flower size, pollinator visitation and mating-system allocation, but antagonist response to the same flower-size coordinate is not measured.

A yellow anther-mimic visual coordinate is manipulated for pollination/fruit set and is borne on petal apices used by florivorous beetles; the florivory link is associational rather than a do(A) response.
Herbivory and cyanogenic defence alter selection on floral traits, but direct pollinator response to the same focal coordinate is not measured.
Flower morphology predicts whether ants act as legitimate visitors or nectar thieves, but no plant reproductive outcome closes the role comparison.
Long tubular corollas and abundant flowering are associated with nectar robbery across a community, but the same-study pollination response and common fitness outcome are absent.

A globelike floral morphology occurs in a dual-role nursery-pollination system with pollination benefit and larval seed cost, but the current audit does not establish a trait-specific response surface for the morphology.
Multiple floral traits, neighborhood context, pollinators and nectar robbers are linked across habitats, but no single common trait coordinate is yet isolated.
Experimental evolution changes a multitrait floral-attraction/defence phenotype under bee and aphid regimes, but no single focal shared coordinate is identified.
Corolla access geometry predicts legitimate versus robbing honeybee behavior and yield across cultivars; the same consumer switches functional role.
Water stress and herbivory induce floral volatile changes that affect bumblebee choice, but herbivores are antecedent treatments rather than receivers of the same floral coordinate.
Flower-size/access geometry is linked to nectar-robbing behavior without a same-coordinate pollinator response or common reproductive endpoint.
Within-tree flowering synchrony is studied in a dual-role pollinating seed-predator system, but no paired receiver-response geometry is identified for the phenology coordinate.
Species-specific floral scent responses are resolved for Epicephala pollinators, but no separate antagonist response to the same code or common fitness outcome is measured.
Female-flower morphology is embedded in a pollinating seed-predator association, but the current source audit does not resolve a same-coordinate component geometry suitable for H1.
Population-differentiated floral morphology is linked to pollination efficacy, Greya oviposition/seed parasitism and seed set across two populations; trait-specific axes must be separated.

Scape length, flower number and petal size are exposed to pollinator and seed-predator/grazer selection on female reproductive success across populations; same Primula farinosa programme as SCHPRISMA-000523.
Petal stickiness is experimentally manipulated and linked to florivory and fruit set, but pollinator response to do(stickiness) is not directly measured.
Identical synthetic scent compounds attract bumblebees and repel ants, but no common plant reproductive outcome links the two receiver responses and ant role is conditional.
